title: William Dawes (ex-governor of Sierra Leone, CMS superintendent, Antigua): letters 'used for cypher' with a key to the cypher
correspondents: William Dawes, CMS superintendent in the West Indies → Church Missionary Society, London (recipient not stated in the catalogue)
place: Antigua (also visited Dominica and St Vincent in 1823)
shelfmark: Cadbury Research Library, Church Missionary Society archive, CMS/B/OMS/C/W/O31 (Dawes, William), items /29 and /30
folio_note: two items in a file of 138; /29 'Letters to used for cypher 1823', /30 'Key to cypher 1823'; extent of cipher text unknown
status: Catalogue description only (Birmingham CalmView, 14 Nov 2026): '/29 Letters to used for cypher 1823; /30 Key to cypher 1823'. why: A missionary society's own cipher with its key, from a man who had governed Sierra Leone: a small sample of how the CMS corresponded in secret in the 1820s (Africa link is the writer's earlier career, the document itself is West Indian).
